title: The width of the bit rotation determines which bits are wrapped
summary: Circularly shift 0x81 to the left by one bit according to the eight-bit width to get 0x03; after ordinary left shift truncation, only 0x02 is obtained.
applies: 64-bit mode for x86-64; Intel SDM Volume 1 and Volume 2
aliases: High level rolls back to low level
detail: ROL/ROR moves the moved bits back to the other end. If the same initial value is circularly shifted to the left by 32 bits, 0x00000102 is obtained.
boundary: RCL/RCR also incorporates the carry flag into the rotation and cannot be directly replaced by the result of ROL/ROR.
relevance: Avoid using native integer width rotations when recalculating byte-wise encoding transformations.
